chunks: A number of our companions, from Ahmad ibn Muhammad, from al-Husayn ibn Sa'id, from Fadalah ibn Ayyub, from Sayf ibn 'Amira, from 'Abdullah ibn 'Abdullah, from a man, from Abu Ja'far (peace be upon him), who said:

The Messenger of God (peace be upon him and his family) said, when the month of Ramadan arrived — and that was with three days remaining from Sha'ban — he said to Bilal: 'Call out among the people'. So he gathered the people. Then he ascended the pulpit, praised God and extolled Him, then said:

'O people! Indeed this month — God has singled you out with it and it has come to you, and it is the master of the months. There is a night in it better than a thousand months; in it the gates of the Fire are locked and the gates of the Gardens are opened. So whoever reaches it and is not forgiven, may God remove him far. And whoever finds his parents alive and is not forgiven, may God remove him far. And whoever has me mentioned in his presence and does not send blessings upon me — God will not forgive him, and may God remove him far.'

key_terms.أَبْوَابُ النَّارِ: The gates of the Fire (Hell) — locked during Ramadan symbolizing reduced power of evil
key_terms.أَبْوَابُ الْجِنَانِ: The gates of the Gardens (Paradise) — opened during Ramadan symbolizing heightened divine mercy
key_terms.سَيِّدُ الشُّهُورِ: The master/chief of the months — a title for Ramadan expressing its supreme rank among all months
key_terms.فَأَبْعَدَهُ اللَّهُ: May God remove him far — a prophetic malediction, expressing profound spiritual distance from divine mercy
key_terms.لَيْلَةُ الْقَدْرِ: The Night of Decree (implied) — the unnamed night better than a thousand months, referring to Laylat al-Qadr

ai.seo_question: What did the Prophet Muhammad say about Ramadan in his sermon just before the month began?
ai.summary: This hadith records Imam al-Baqir (AS) transmitting a sermon of the Prophet (SAWW) delivered on the minbar just before Ramadan began, in which the Prophet emphasized the unparalleled sanctity of the month. The sermon was addressed to the assembled Muslim community in Medina with an urgent call to seize the opportunity for forgiveness, underscoring three categories of people for whom this blessed season yields no benefit due to their own failures: one who reaches Ramadan without being forgiven, one who has living parents but fails to earn their blessing, and one who does not send salawat upon the Prophet when his name is mentioned.

en.hubeali:
A number of our companions, from Ahmad Bin Muhammad, from Al Husayn Bin Saeed, from Fazalat Bin Ayoub, from Sayf Bin Ameyra, from Abdullah Bin Abdullah, from a man, 
(It has been narrated) from Abu Ja’far<sup>asws</sup> having said:

‘Rasool-Allah<sup>saww</sup> said, when the Month of Ramazan presented itself, and that was when there remained three days from Sha’ban, said to Bilal: ‘Call out among the people’. So the people gathered. Then he<sup>saww</sup> ascended the Pulpit, so he<sup>saww</sup> Praised Allah<sup>azwj</sup> and Extolled upon Him<sup>azwj</sup>, then said:

‘O you people! This is the Month which Allah<sup>azwj</sup> has Chosen you all with, and it is presenting itself, and it is the chief of the months. 
There is a night therein better than a thousand months, in which the doors of the Fire are locked, and in which the doors of the Gardens are opened up. So the one who realises it, and there is no Forgiveness for him, so Allah<sup>azwj</sup> has Made him to be remote; and the one has his parents, and there is no Forgiveness for him, so Allah<sup>azwj</sup> has Made him to be remote; and the one in whose presence I<sup>saww</sup> am mentioned and he does not send Blessing upon me<sup>saww</sup>, so Allah<sup>azwj</sup> will not Forgive him, and Allah<sup>azwj</sup> Makes him to be remote’.
en.sarwar: 5. A number of our people have narrated from Ahmad ibn Muhammad, from al-Husayn ibn Sa‘id from, Fadalah ibn Ayyub from Sayf ibn ‘Ami rah from ‘ Abd Allah ibn ‘ Abd Allah from a man who has said the following: ”Abu Ja’far, ‘Alayhi al-Salam, has said that the Messenger of Allah, O Allah, grant compensation to Muhammad and his family worthy of their services to Your cause, once, just three days before the month of Ramadan, said to Bilal, ‘Call people (to come to the Masjid).’ People then gathered, and he climbed on the pulpit, thanked Allah, praised Him, and then said, “O people, Allah has granted you a privilege with this month. He has made it especially for you, and it is about to be upon you. There is one night in it that is better than one thousand months. The doors of hell fire remain closed in this month, and the doors of Paradise are open. If one’s sins remain without being forgiven in this month, Allah keeps him away. One who lives with his parents, but is not forgiven, Allah keeps him away; and one before whom I am mentioned but who does not say salawat (O Allah, grant compensation to Muhammad and his family worthy of their services to your cause) and is not forgiven, Allah keeps him away.’”
